request: Create an AXI4-Lite timer peripheral with an interrupt.
expected_behavior: RTL for module axil_timer (AXI4-Lite subordinate, ADDR_WIDTH 4 by default and 4 to 8 allowed, 32-bit data) with CTRL (EN, IE, MODE), LOAD, a read-only COUNT and a write-1-to-clear STATUS at 0x0 to 0xC, one-shot and periodic counts of exactly LOAD cycles, a level irq, and a self-checking testbench, following the approved interface specification and microarchitecture, gated by lint, simulation, and synthesis (and formal, when a .sby is written) before review.
constraints: Work only from the approved interface specification and microarchitecture.
Correct for every ADDR_WIDTH from 4 to 8: offsets 0x10 and up are unmapped.
Lint-clean under Verilator -Wall with no waivers.
known_failure_modes: A one-shot count that reloads and runs on, or whose EN never clears itself.
A periodic period one cycle long or short, or a first period that differs from the rest.
A write of EN 0 that does not stop a running count.
An acknowledgement that wipes out an expiry landing on the same edge.
Offsets 0x10 and above aliasing the registers when ADDR_WIDTH is above 4.
A self-written testbench that never times a count to the cycle; the held-out reference testbench judges instead.
A self-written testbench that cannot tell a one-shot that runs on, an off-by-one reload, an ignored stop or an aliased decode from a correct timer; the must-fail control fails it.

held_out.name: The reference testbench passes on the seat's RTL
The seat's testbench fails each timer mutant
The case's ADDR_WIDTH 8 proof reaches every cover and fails each mutant
The case's ADDR_WIDTH 4 proof reaches every cover and fails each mutant wrong at ADDR_WIDTH 4
